title: Berlin woolwork parrot panel
subtitle: A small framed panel of a perched parrot worked from a Victorian charted design in tent stitch
excerpt: The perched parrot is one of the most common Victorian Berlin woolwork subjects. This small panel works a single parrot in nine shades on a dark background in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas. Finished size is 18 by 23 cm.
sourceNotes: Parrot motif from Weldon's Practical Needlework, Berlin work series (1887). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), parrot and bird subjects chapter. Mrs Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746.

glossaryTerms.definition: A needlepoint design printed on squared paper in which each square represents one tent stitch, used to produce detailed bird subjects in a range of colours on canvas.

heroPrompt: A framed needlepoint panel showing a brightly coloured parrot on a perch, Victorian Berlin work style, jewel colours on dark background, period gilt frame, natural museum light.

content.text: This panel reproduces a Victorian
charted bird motif

of a perched parrot from Weldon's Berlin work series. The design is 94 by 120 holes on 13-count canvas, finishing at 18 by 23 cm. Nine shades of green, yellow, red, and grey shade the plumage and perch. The background is dark navy.

content.text: Palette
Wing dark: DMC 890 / Anchor 218: ultra dark pistachio green
Wing medium: DMC 987 / Anchor 244: dark forest green
Wing light: DMC 989 / Anchor 242: forest green
Chest yellow: DMC 726 / Anchor 295: light topaz
Breast red: DMC 817 / Anchor 13: very dark coral red
Head: DMC 745 / Anchor 300: light pale yellow
Beak: DMC 414 / Anchor 235: dark steel grey
Perch: DMC 433 / Anchor 358: medium brown
Eye: DMC 310 / Anchor 403: black
Background: DMC 336 / Anchor 150: navy blue
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a scroll frame. A panel of this size needs a stable working surface; the large navy background area distorts in a hoop.
Stitches used
Basketweave tent stitch
throughout.
Working method
Mark the design boundary and draw a 10-hole reference grid on the canvas in pencil.
Work the parrot motif first. Start with the perch and work the bird's feet, then the body. Work from the bottom of the bird upward: perch, feet, lower body, wings, chest, head, beak, eye.
Shade the plumage: darker shades at the wing edges and upper body, lighter shades on the chest and inner areas.
Fill the navy background in basketweave. Work around the motif carefully to avoid crossing into the design stitches.
Block the finished canvas by dampening and pinning square to a board overnight.
Finishing
Lace the blocked canvas over the acid-free mounting board and fit into a picture frame. A gilt or dark mahogany frame suits the Victorian period character of the design.
What to try next
A peacock or tropical butterfly uses the same multi-shade plumage technique. Both subjects appear in Victorian Berlin work charts and benefit from the same navy or black background.
